content:
In France, the social security system means that care before and after birth is completely paid for in public hospitals. Women in salaried jobs can also take 16 weeks of maternity leave, receiving between €9.29 and €84.90 per day, depending on their previous earnings.

During pregnancy and the period surrounding birth, money is generally not a new concern: families already in difficulty continue to struggle, while wealthier families remain comfortable. But when it comes to practical support for new mothers, very little is provided. Paternity leave is just 11 days, far too short to allow mothers enough time to recover after giving birth.

As a result, new mothers are left to cope with the constant demands of caring for a baby while still healing themselves. They also have to find childcare, even though public options are limited, particularly around Paris. Costs differ widely. Public daycare can cost lower-income families about €1,000 a year, but availability is scarce, with only one spot for every eight children. Many families are therefore forced to rely on private options, such as childminders or in-home care. Any other questions?
